components.description: Signature: source number through a glass prism into spectral part chips; rays draw and chips fan in.
components.html: 3830+8
components.css: .ds-prism{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;padding:12px;background:#fff}.ds-prism .src,.ds-prism .chip{font-family:'Manrope',system-ui,sans-serif;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;font-weight:700;font-size:19px;padding:6px 12px;border-radius:12px}.ds-prism .src{background:rgba(255,255,255,.85);border:1px solid rgba(28,36,84,.1);box-shadow:0 4px 10px -6px rgba(24,32,88,.3);color:#141833}.ds-prism .chip{color:var(--pc);background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--pc) 9%,rgba(255,255,255,.85));border:1px solid color-mix(in srgb,var(--pc) 28%,transparent);box-shadow:0 6px 14px -8px color-mix(in srgb,var(--pc) 60%,transparent);animation:dsfan .6s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both}.ds-prism .op{font-family:'Manrope',system-ui,sans-serif;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;font-weight:500;font-size:18px;color:#5a6082;animation:dsfan .6s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) both}.ds-prism .ray{fill:none;stroke-linecap:round;stroke-dasharray:1;stroke-dashoffset:1;animation:dsdraw .55s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) forwards}@keyframes dsdraw{to{stroke-dashoffset:0}}@keyframes dsfan{from{opacity:0;transform:translateX(-18px) scale(.92);filter:blur(4px)}to{opacity:1;transform:none;filter:none}}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-prism *{animation-duration:.01ms!important;animation-delay:0s!important}}

narrative.overview:
Every mental-math technique is the act of splitting a number into easy parts, and this system makes that split literal: white light enters a small glass prism and leaves as coloured parts. The interface around it is light liquid glass. Frosted panes sit over a white ground lit by soft, blurred colour pools, and they pick up that colour through backdrop blur and saturation. Nothing is opaque except the text and the one dark primary button.

It is an Operate surface, dense but calm: a sticky glass top bar, a glass rail of techniques, and two working panes side by side. Numbers carry the weight. They are set large and light in Manrope with tabular figures, while Thai UI text runs in Anuphan at ordinary reading sizes. Colour is reserved for meaning: three spectral part colours for decomposed numbers, three level hues for Basic / Intermediate / Advanced, and green/red only for right/wrong.

Motion is orchestration, not decoration. Rays draw, chips fan out, steps rise in sequence, all on one long-tail ease (cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)); the colour field drifts only when the level changes. Reduced-motion users get everything instantly.
keyCharacteristics: Frosted white glass panes (blur 22px, saturate 170%) with a specular top edge and soft lifted shadow.
A fixed light field of five blurred colour pools; two of them take the current level's soft hue.
The Prism Split: source chip → glass prism → coloured part chips, drawn per reveal.
Spectral part roles (blue / orange / magenta) used identically in chips, step text, rays, number-line arcs and area models.
Manrope tabular figures for every number; Anuphan for every Thai word.
One stroke-icon family (1.8px, round caps) authored as inline SVG symbols.

rules.name: The Spectral Roles Rule
rules.body: A decomposed part is always blue, then orange, then magenta, in that order, everywhere it appears: chip, ray, step text, arc, area-model label. Never use these three for chrome, status or level.

rules.name: The Colour Means Something Rule
rules.body: Level hues mark level, green/red mark correctness, part colours mark parts. Panes, buttons and the bar are white glass or ink; none of them takes an accent fill.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: Every number (problems, chips, steps, stats, beads count, scores, SVG labels) is Manrope with `tnum`. Thai text is never set in Manrope, and numbers are never set in Anuphan.

rules.name: The Light Problem Rule
rules.body: Problems are thin (300) and large; weight is spent only on the answer once revealed and on part chips.

rules.name: The Glass Needs Light Rule
rules.body: Glass panes only sit over the coloured field. Never put a glass pane on flat ground or over another glass pane; nested surfaces are brighter opaque-ish white, not another blur layer.

rules.name: The Soft Lift Rule
rules.body: All drops are soft, negative-spread and indigo-tinted. No hard offset shadows, no pure-black shadows.

dos: **Do** colour every decomposed part by its spectral role (blue, orange, magenta in order), identically in chips, rays, steps, arcs and area models.
**Do** set every number in Manrope with tabular figures, and every Thai string in Anuphan.
**Do** place glass panes over the coloured light field, with blur(22px) saturate(170%), a 1px white edge and the Glass Pane shadow.
**Do** tint the field and level markers with the current level's hue (teal / amber / violet); fall back to ink and periwinkle when no level applies.
**Do** keep one ink primary button per pane; everything else is secondary glass or ghost.
**Do** run motion on cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) with staggered delays, and honour prefers-reduced-motion.
**Do** draw icons as single-stroke inline SVG (1.8px, round caps and joins, 18px).
donts: **Don't** use the part colours for buttons, status, levels or decoration.
**Don't** stack glass on glass or put glass over flat ground.
**Don't** use hard offset or black shadows; lifts are soft and indigo-tinted.
**Don't** add accent-filled panes or a grey sidebar; panes and rail stay white glass.
**Don't** let the prism row wrap; it scrolls instead.
**Don't** use icon fonts, emoji or glyph characters as icons.
